blocks.content: No — they're independent. Looking at the `WindowTitleBar.svelte` layout:

<WorkspaceViewModeToggle />
{#if $workspaceViewMode$ === 'single'}
  <WorkspaceTabStrip ... />
  <WorkspaceRepoLauncher />
{/if}
{#if $workspaceViewMode$ === 'columns'}
  {@render titlebarUtilities(false)}
{/if}
...
<!-- Right column: global status and settings -->
{#if $workspaceViewMode$ === 'single'}
  {@render titlebarUtilities(true)}
{/if}

In the normal single (tab) view — which is what onboarding uses — the daemon status indicator and settings button live in a **separate right-side block** (`titlebarUtilities(true)`), completely outside the left workspace-controls container. Hiding the view toggle, the "+" button, or even the whole tab strip does not touch them.

The one caveat: in **columns** view mode, the settings button is rendered inside the left controls container (`titlebarUtilities(false)`). That's why the spec task deliberately hides only the two specific components (`WorkspaceViewModeToggle` and `WorkspaceRepoLauncher`) rather than the entire `data-titlebar-workspace-controls` container — so the settings button would survive even in that mode. Daemon status only renders in single mode either way.

So with the plan as written: view toggle and "+" disappear during onboarding; daemon status and settings stay visible. Ready to delegate on your approval.
